lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The warning lights flickered in Calgary, but the Leafs' season is hardly veering off the road. Toronto's 5-2 loss to the Flames snapped its winning run and exposed the familiar flaw: careless turnovers followed by soft defensive coverage. Easton Cowan took the blame for a bad giveaway and a needless penalty, yet he also scored Toronto's first goal and remained one of its liveliest forwards. The kid's accountability is admirable; making him the scapegoat would be lazy. At 7-5, Toronto sits third in the Eastern Conference with 16 points, three behind the lead, and one loss does not erase the emphatic 7-2 demolition of Edmonton two nights earlier. General manager John Chayka says defensive improvement need not require a trade, though the need is plain. The next test comes Wednesday in Seattle at 10 p.m. ET, where the Leafs must defend better and halt this one-game skid.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and the lesson arriving from the Brewers and Rays is as blunt as a fastball under the hands: October rewards pitching depth, clean baseball and relentless pressure. Toronto's immediate task is finding a left-handed starter - Trevor Rogers has emerged as a possible target, a sensible answer for a rotation that cannot enter 2027 relying on health and hope. The Blue Jays finished 79-83, second in the AL East, but the record is only the starting point; the larger failure was an offense that vanished when the roster needed it most. Ernie Clement's engagement party before his World Series appearance offers a lighter reminder that Toronto still has useful, human pieces, while the Arizona Fall League provides a glimpse at the next wave. Watch the front office pursue rotation help and a dependable bat before camp opens - because next year requires construction, not consolation.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A promising start hit its first hard wall in Minneapolis. The Raptors' 117-94 loss to the Timberwolves exposed how thin Toronto's margin becomes without Kawhi Leonard, sidelined by knee swelling, and how badly Scottie Barnes must answer that absence. Barnes went 0-for-12 from the field, a shocking blank from the team's leading scorer, though he still supplied four steals. One bad night does not erase a 2-1 start, but it does explain the Raptors' current L1 streak and their precarious perch - second in the Atlantic, just 0.5 games behind. The larger question now echoes around the organization: was choosing Leonard over LaMelo Ball the right bet, and can Barnes carry it when Leonard cannot? Wednesday's 7:30 p.m. home date with Orlando is the immediate referendum - watch whether Barnes attacks early and whether Leonard's knee keeps him out.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The bye week did not erase Washington's problems; it sharpened them. Terry McLaurin's season-ending torn patellar tendon now leaves the Commanders asking Stefon Diggs, rookie Antonio Williams and a returning Treylon Burks to rebuild the passing game. That is a brutal assignment for a team sitting 1-4-1, third in the NFC East and 2.5 games back, with a loss and a tie in its last two outings. Jayden Daniels is still finding his stride after the elbow injury that interrupted his season, and the offense cannot afford another quiet stretch. The news is mixed elsewhere: Marcus Mariota and Charles Omenihu are expected back at practice, while Javon Kinlaw's knee recovery is lagging. Washington remains in contention, but the margin has narrowed to a thread. Sunday night's 8:20 p.m. meeting with Philadelphia is the hinge point: beat the Eagles, and the chase lives; lose, and the season's ambitions become largely theoretical.

article.title: Leafs Lose to Flames as Cowan Takes Blame
paragraphs: The Leafs lost 5-2 to the Flames on Monday, despite goals from Easton Cowan and William Nylander. Cowan also blamed himself for a turnover and penalty, while Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 29 shots. Toronto is 7-5 and visits the Kraken Wednesday at 10:00 p.m. ET on Sportsnet.

The Blue Jays are turning toward the offseason, with left-handed pitching among the early questions. Ernie Clement, meanwhile, held an engagement party before his World Series appearance. The Raptors are 2-1 and host the Magic Wednesday at 7:30 p.m., with Scottie Barnes' play drawing attention. The Commanders, 1-4-1, host the Eagles Sunday at 8:20 p.m. on NBC, with the stakes high in Washington.
